messages:
SLO-bot: ALERT hosted-infer-prod: p99 latency breached 5s, SLO burn 18% over 10m, 5xx rate spike (gateway) :warning:
Ali: seeing customer tickets about timeouts/502s. getting several from enterprise accounts. can someone grab traces and a sample request id? :eyes:
Ben: looking now — an uptick in 502/504 from gateway-to-batcher path. backend pool threads at 96% in last 5m, lots of keepalive resets. grabbing logs for request ids that match 502 pattern.
Cam: dashboard -> https://ops.redwood/dashboard/d/ingress/hosted-infer?panel=5 shows p99 jump at 14:02 UTC. trace sampling shows partial traces with missing spans from edge-proxy -> model-host (trace gap). probable span-drop at the gateway side.
Dana: support got an enterprise escalation (acme) reporting repeated 502s around 14:01–14:05, example request_id=req_7f2a2c. Attached their example: `POST /v1/generate` with ~4k token prompt.
Ben: repro run with their request_id in logs: found gateway returned 502 after 30s backend timeout. The batcher reported a worker eviction: `killed-for-latency` when sequence len + kv-prep exceeded worker_budget.
Ali: can you paste the exact query you ran to pull those request logs? I want to check correlating metrics (connections, tcp resets).
Ben: sure — log query:
```
source:gateway AND status:502 AND request_id:req_7f2a2c | sort by @timestamp desc | limit 200
```
also tcp reset grep on edge proxies:
```
sudo journalctl -u edge-proxy | grep \"RST\" | grep \"req_7f2a2c\" -A 5 -B 5
```
results: ~120 RSTs in window, client side saw connection close before backend response.
Cam: trace query I used (jaeger-like):
```
trace.service:\"gateway\" AND trace.tags.request_id:\"req_7f2a2c\" | show spans | group by span.name
```
there are gaps after `gateway.forward_to_batcher` — no `batcher.exec` span for many traces. suggests requests were dropped by connection reset before batcher processed.
Dana: customer Slack says they had a series of 6 similar requests that failed then one succeeded after retry. sequence length was large & contains embedded json. good to know for repro.
Ali: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) relax gateway backend timeout from 30s -> 45s for hosted-infer route for canary, 2) temporarily increase batcher worker pool for hosted-infer, 3) enable per-route prefix caching to reduce long seq prefill. which is least invasive?
Ben: increasing worker pool + scaling group is fastest. changing timeouts is risky since it can tie up workers. I'll spin up +30% worker replicas in the pool and watch.
Cam: I'll enable higher trace sampling for the next 15m and add a synthetic probe that issues long-prompt requests to the canary queue to reproduce locally. also updating dashboard panels for `span_missing:gateway->batcher` metric.
Ali: action items: Ben -> scale pool (assigned), Cam -> increase trace sampling + probe, Dana -> reply to customer with expected ETA and ask for full curl + request headers, Ben/Cam -> collect full traces & tcp dump if possible. I'll watch SLO burn and escalate to infra if no improvement in 10m. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: started scale operation: hosted-infer-batcher +3 replicas (job id deploy-8102).
Ben: scale done. initial metrics: backend threads back to 45% within 60s. 502 rate falling but still above baseline. continuing to ingest traces.
Cam: got a tcpdump from one edge node that shows SYN, SYN-ACK, then repeated RST after ~28s. correlates exactly with gateway timeout. looks like clients aborting after 30s.
Ali: interesting — clients aborting at ~30s suggests upstream timeout policy might be closing earlier than batcher. need to align keepalive and client timeouts and ensure long-prompt paths have increased deadline.
Dana: told acme we'll do an ETA of 1h and suggested short-term retry/backoff. they accepted.
Ben: next steps I think: 1) patch gateway timeout config to 45s for hosted-infer route (canary), 2) add worker budget telemetry by sequence-length buckets, 3) improve prefix-cache prefill so large prompts don't occupy workers for entire prefill time.
Cam: i'll open a dashboard PR and add a saved query for `trace_gap:gateway->batcher` and wire an alert if gap rate > 5% for 5m.
Ali: sounds good. I'll keep this thread updated. If we hit >30% SLO burn I'll pagedown infra.
Dana: thanks team — letting customer know we have a mitigation in flight. :white_check_mark:
SLO-bot: UPDATE hosted-infer-prod: p99 4.9s, SLO burn down to 7% in last 5m.
Ali: closing loop for now. will follow up with long-term fixes in next infra retro.
